items.title: UK FCA’s supervisory spotlight is fixed on financial crime: firms should review systems and controls now
items.description: The FCA’s September 2026 Regulation Round-Up includes a feature piece by Steve Smart, FCA Executive Director of Enforcement and Market Oversight and lead for fighting financial crime. The article emphasises the ‘vital’ importance of firms’ readiness to combat financial crime as it continues to grow in scale, sophistication and impact. It also outlines recent and planned FCA activity in this area. The combined message of this work is clear: the FCA is honing its strategic focus on fighting financial crime and could well be looking to further demonstrate the power of its technology-enabled, data-led approach through more supervisory and enforcement action in the not-too-distant future. In anticipation of such action, firms would be wise to carefully consider the FCA’s recent publications – including the findings from its multi-firm review of money mule activity – and carry out a comprehensive evaluation of their financial crime systems and controls, strengthening them where necessary. In this article, we set out key takeaways from some of the FCA’s most recent publications, including a few suggested next steps for firms.

items.description: The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has published two pieces of final non-Handbook guidance explaining how firms within its new prudential regime for regulated cryptoasset activities should approach their obligation under the FCA Handbook to perform an overall risk assessment: FG26/9 on COREPRU 7 and FG26/10 on CRYPTOPRU 7. The guidance describes how firms should evaluate their business models, risks and resource needs in order to maintain adequate financial resources to continue operating or, if necessary, to wind down without causing material harm to customers or the UK market. It is illustrative and non-exhaustive and does not impose a single methodology. Both publications take effect on 25 October 2027.

items.title: ESG Focus: UK/EU/International ESG Regulation Monthly Round-Up – August/September 2026
items.description: We took a brief summer break but are back with this edition of the ESG Regulation Monthly Round-Up covering developments from the UK, EU and internationally during August and September 2026.Generally there have been a lot of developments around corporate sustainability reporting in the UK, EU, Australia, New Zealand and California. The direction of travel seems to be a recalibration of mandatory expectations on companies. There have also been a number of conversations and plans announced around adaptation and resilience – which is a leading topic as we head to the end of 2026.

items.title: Injunctions against bond calls: A reminder of the high threshold - TTSJV V BAPCO
items.description: Performance bonds (or performance guarantees) are the “lifeblood of international commerce” and the English courts remain reluctant to intervene when a beneficiary seeks to call on one. In TTSJV WLL & Ors v BapCo Refining BSC [2026] EWHC 2047 (TCC), the Technology and Construction Court refused an urgent application to suspend a demand on a US$484 million performance guarantee arising from a delayed US$4.2 billion oil refinery modernisation project in Bahrain. The decision clarifies the very high threshold that must be met to prevent beneficiaries from calling on performance guarantees and provides useful guidance on the interaction between court intervention and emergency arbitration.

items.description: The primary time limit to bring a claim in the employment tribunal has increased today (1 October 2026), from three to six months.
